limitations: Local isolated PostgreSQL dump/restore drill; managed production backups, scheduling, encryption at rest and off-site storage were not exercised.
Database restoration retains image references; S3/object files require their own backup and restore drill.
checks: Current migrations and exact nine-product seed applied to a new isolated source database
Synthetic COD order, historic prices, administrator hash, image metadata and audit record created only in drill database
Production backup script created a valid custom-format archive with owner-only file permissions
The explicit source URL takes precedence over inherited libpq service selectors
Backup script rejects overwriting an existing archive without modifying its bytes
Failed database connection leaves no final backup or partial archive
Restoration requires explicit empty-target confirmation before making changes
Restoration refuses a nonempty target and leaves all source rows unchanged
Invalid archive is rejected without creating tables in the target
Restoration also refuses an otherwise empty database containing a custom schema without removing it
Every restored public table matches the source row count and full row-content SHA256
COD payment, order history and original 75 + 20 = 95 ILS snapshots survive restoration alongside newer catalog prices
Restored private administrator credential hash verifies the correct password and rejects a wrong password
Restored image URL and original key still resolve to the separately preserved local media assets
Secure tracking and idempotent retry function on the restored database without exposing PII or creating a second order
Redeploy migrations and seed preserve the restored order and administrative price changes
